Twenty comments

The Last Pint

Is it a hornpipe or is it a reel? I’m not quite sure.

I saw the ABCs for this tune on the IRTRAD-l mailing list (always a good source of tunes and tune-lore) and I remembered that Lunasa fans had been hoping to see this one on The Session. Enjoy!

↳ Posted by Jeremy on August 3rd, 2001.

It’s a hornpipe

I think this was written by Pierre Bensusan, playing hornpipes like hornpipes is out of favor nowadays. That’s probably what caused the confusion.

↳ Posted by b.maloney on August 3rd, 2001.

Its a reel

(in my opinion!) Yes it was written by Pierre Bensusan and is on his album . The original key is F

↳ Posted by sallyg on July 14th, 2002.

Is it missing a variation? I’m no great shakes at hearing notea and reading music but I think there’s something missing when compared to Lunasa’s recording of it.

↳ Posted by Bothysix on December 28th, 2004.

This tune was originally a Reel then Lunasa slowed it down. It is a nice tune. I believe the original key is Bb which is how it would sound up a minor third or on an F Whistle or Flute.

↳ Posted by Avery on December 23rd, 2005.

Just saw Lunasa perform “Like A Pint” in Bb

I just enjoyed seeing Lunasa live in concert at the Gibson Showcase here in Nashville, and managed to record bits and pieces of it on my iPod. My favorite song of the evening was “Like a Pint” and as soon as I got into my car, I turned on the iPod, grabbed my whistles and figured it out… Sure enough they performed it in Bb on a low F whistle, and by the time I got home, I had most of the basics down (not nearly as beautiflully as Lunasa does it, but at least a decent start!) Anyway I can confirm that they did it in the key of Bb on a low F whistle, or more accurately on THREE low F whistles!

I’ve also seen this performed with 3 whistles- with the A fingering on a Bb whistle, G fingering on a C whistle, and D fingering on an F whistle - putting it in the key of F, though I don’t remember which one(s) were high and low whistles, respectively (maybe a C, Bb and low F)?

For the key of G, I guess that would likely be a C, high or low D, and low G?

Not sure how Lunasa has it in Bb/F and has more than one low whistle - might have a baritone low C, or bass Bb, though low (tenor) D is the bottom end for most of us?

The Last Pint - the ‘jazz variation’

I see that several people have added the first variation - |BcBG cdcG|BcBG ded2| etc - but what about the slow improv on that itself which they play before returning for the last time thru. It’s all crotchets, and the two whistles weave in and out of each other. There’s an ostinato figure for 2 bars, done in unison, and then it goes into 8 bars of improv. Again there 2 parts. I’ve sort of worked out the higher, ‘lead’ part, but the lower whistle part is more subtle and harder to discern from the other, a they are occasionally playing in unison for a note or two, it seems.

Here’s what I have got

T: The Last Pint final variation
S: Lunasa
R: hornpipe
L: 1/8
M: 4/4
K: Gmaj

|e2d2 e2d2 | B6 b2 |a2 g2 g2 f2 | g2 f2 f2 e2 |e2 d2 B2 A2||G8 |

has anyone transcribed that lower part ?
